title: Postoperative Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Critical Management Guide
summary: Postoperative upper gastrointestinal (UGI) bleeding is a life-threatening complication necessitating rapid stabilization, multispecialty coordination, and precise endoscopic intervention. This guide outlines the evidence-based approach to the unstable surgical patient.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Scope
sections.content: Postoperative UGI bleeding refers to hemorrhage originating from the esophagus, stomach, or duodenum occurring within 30 days post-surgery. It is distinct from pre-existing conditions, often exacerbated by systemic stress, coagulopathy, and pharmacological factors.

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Stabilization
content: Hematemesis (bright red blood) or Coffee-ground emesis
Melena (tarry, black stools indicating >50mL blood loss)
Signs of hypovolemic shock (cool/clammy skin, oliguria)

rows: Anastomotic bleeding, Dieulafoy’s lesion, Aorto-enteric fistula

sections.title: Initial Resuscitation Protocol
content: Step 1: Secure two large-bore (16-18G) IV lines.
Step 2: Crystalloid fluid resuscitation (Goal: MAP > 65 mmHg).
Step 3: Transfuse PRBCs if Hb < 7 g/dL (or < 9 g/dL in high-risk cardiac patients).
Step 4: Reverse coagulopathy (FFP, Platelets, Vitamin K as indicated).
Step 5: Initiate IV PPI bolus (80mg) followed by infusion (8mg/hr).

sections.title: Endoscopic Intervention Modalities
content: Injection: Epinephrine (1:10,000 dilution) to induce vasoconstriction.
Mechanical: Endoclips for visible vessels or active spurting.
Topical: Hemospray (hemostatic powder) for diffuse oozing.

content.mnemonic: IA, IB, IIA, IIB, IIC, III
content.explanation: IA: Spurting, IB: Oozing (High risk). IIA: Visible vessel, IIB: Adherent clot. IIC: Hematin-covered base, III: Clean base (Low risk).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: PPIs reduce the need for surgery but do not improve mortality directly.
Early endoscopy (within 24 hours) is mandatory for hemodynamically stabilized patients.
Always check INR/PT/PTT; surgical patients are often on prophylactic anticoagulation.
Consult Interventional Radiology (IR) early if endoscopic attempts fail.
